current_answer: As of 8 October 2026, public evidence still does not establish a broad capability decline across popular AI models or a confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 regression. One 1 October GitHub issue in Anthropic's Claude Code repository reports higher Opus 5.5 High thinking tokens (67 to 126 median per request) and output tokens (447 to 711) between 29 earlier sessions and 8 sessions on 1 October. The author reports worse judgment and a same-day issue in claude.ai, but the CLI changed from 2.1.282–2.1.285 to 2.1.286 on the comparison date, tasks were not matched, and outputs or a controlled replay are not available in the issue. Treat it as a testable one-account signal, not a model-side or broad decline finding. OpenAI separately marked Dot/Work errors, APAC service errors, and GPT-5.6 Instant errors in FedRAMP workspaces recovered; those are service or execution records, not quality tests. LiveNerf reports 15/30 daily collections and no post-baseline comparison. Suggested: save the task, exact client/CLI, effort, context, output, and token receipt, then compare matched runs with client changes controlled before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Did Claude Opus 5.5 change on 1 October?
catalogue_card.text: One user reports higher thinking and output tokens, but the CLI changed on the same date. No model decline is confirmed.

summary: No broad capability decline across popular AI models or confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 regression is established by the reviewed public evidence.

A 1 October issue reports higher Opus 5.5 High thinking-token and output-token medians in one user’s sessions. The comparison is not task-matched, and Claude Code CLI 2.1.286 appears only on the post-change date.
The author reports worse task judgment and similar same-day claude.ai symptoms, but the issue has no quality rubric, visible output set, provider confirmation, or independent replication.

OpenAI marked Dot errors in Codex/Work, an APAC issue across Work/conversations/GPTs, and GPT-5.6 Instant errors in FedRAMP workspaces recovered. These are service or execution records, not answer-quality tests.

LiveNerf reports 15/30 collections and no post-baseline comparison. Its pre-registration describes a corrected cutoff and regression test; the available code snapshot is too old to verify the current implementation.

Suggested: check service and region for errors; for a completed answer that seems worse, record the task, effort, context, client/CLI version, output, correction work, and token receipt. Compare matched runs with the client held constant before switching.
uncertainty: The Opus 5.5 token comparison is one author’s local session analysis (29 earlier sessions versus 8 on 1 October); CLI version and date changed together, task mix was not matched, and the linked session-metrics gist could not be fetched in this check.
The issue reports worse judgment and same-day claude.ai symptoms, but provides no controlled task-quality baseline or independent reproduction; the stated p-values do not isolate a model-side cause.
OpenAI status entries are aggregate provider records. They do not establish individual account impact, completed-answer quality, or connection to the Opus 5.5 report.

LiveNerf reports 15 of 30 daily runs and no comparison result. Its pre-registration says the cutoff was corrected and tested, but the available analysis-code page was crawled six days before this check, so current code execution is not independently verified.
LiveNerf measures one Claude Code subscription path and a fixed academic panel, not consumer chat or all user workflows; a first two-window decision is not expected before about 24 October.
Analytics and reader outcomes are unavailable, so the report’s suggested action is not a verified reader action.
freshness_note: Checked 8 October 2026. A detailed but uncontrolled Opus 5.5 token-use report and separate recovered OpenAI service events are new signals; neither establishes broad capability decline. LiveNerf has no comparison result.
